references.text: The context of this verse: Jesus sends Peter and John to prepare the Passover meal, giving them detailed instructions on how to find the room. [ref:Luk 22:8-13|Luke 22:8-13] describes the entire sequence where the disciples are told to follow a man carrying a water jar and ask the homeowner for the guest room.

The parallel passage in the Gospel of Mark. [ref:Mark 14:14-15|Mark 14:14-15] gives almost identical words where Jesus instructs the disciples to say to the homeowner: "The Teacher asks: Where is the room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?"

The parallel passage in the Gospel of Matthew. [ref:Matt 26:17-19|Matthew 26:17-19] tells about the preparation of the Passover meal, although Matthew presents Jesus' instructions in a somewhat shorter form than Luke and Mark.

The Greek word "κατάλυμα" (guest room/inn) is also used in [ref:Luk 2:7|Luke 2:7], where it is told that there was no place for them in the inn when Jesus was born. Luke uses the same word to describe a lodging place both at the beginning and at the end of Jesus' earthly ministry.

The Passover meal has its origin in [ref:2 Mos 12:3-6|Exodus 12:3-6], where God gives the Israelites instructions on how to prepare the Passover lamb. Here Jesus follows Jewish tradition by preparing the celebration of Passover (τὸ πάσχα) with his disciples.

[ref:5 Mos 16:5-6|Deuteronomy 16:5-6] gives regulations about where the Passover meal should be held – it must be eaten at the place the Lord chooses. Jesus demonstrates his sovereign authority by designating the specific place where the meal is to take place.

Jesus is referred to as "The Teacher" (ὁ διδάσκαλος). In [ref:Joh 13:13|John 13:13] Jesus himself confirms this title: "You call me Teacher and Lord, and you are right, for that is what I am." The use of this title in connection with the Passover meal emphasizes Jesus' authority.
